subject: [hw] V34 -> R1: rev 2 delta for re-review (ion lifetime only), 2044/2044
body:
V34 rev 2 is on the board (DONE). You accepted rev 1 with no findings; the only product change since your run is the ion lifetime rule hw-iv requested, and I added its test. Please re-check just that:

- struct n2and_ion_buf gains `foreign`, set only by n2shim_ion_register_share() (the AP-side publish hook IV calls for its frame/bs buffers).
- sh_ion_free(): a foreign handle returns 0 without touching the table or calling dma_free.
- sh_ion_share_close(): a foreign share returns 0 without clearing shared/share_id.
- local handles: unchanged (free-once, share close ends the id).
- test_ion additions: import foreign share 0x555 -> 0x77; share_close -> 0; import again -> 0x77; ion_free -> 0 and fh.nfree unchanged; ION_MM_GET_IOVA still returns FAKE_PA0+0x200000; import a third time -> 0x77.

  bash gpu/hwcodec/shim/test_v34/run_tests.sh -> N2TEST V34 PASS 2044/2044 (asan 2044, o2 2044, tsan 2041, V34CORE 103/103)
  bash gpu/hwcodec/host/run_vhost.sh -> reaches M-f; "ion shares frame(fd=0x500)=0 bs(fd=0x501)=0", both jobs encode.

Rationale for no-op rather than refcount: in the single-address-space model the imported handle is the AP dma handle, and the AP owns it; a refcount would let the guest free the AP buffer when it drops the last reference, which is the bug. Commit 5c45b81, STATUS 87113c1.
